findings.statement: Must fix before design handoff: R9-19/20 does not explicitly require newly measured radiation-jet uncertainty to be part of the calibrated joint inclusion event. A jet law and same-state/frame mapping alone do not let JOINT_SET retain its confidence level after augmenting it with new uncertain derivatives.

reproduction: Two independent 95% regions for preexisting state and new jet variables have joint inclusion probability .95^2=.9025; taking their identity image does not restore .95.

Require either jet/nuisance variables already included in the same calibrated event, or an augmented common region with a prospective joint error allocation/calibration. With neither, physical output remains conditional/scenario/unavailable; do not recycle spent alpha.

findings.statement: D1-D4 and F1-F3 correctly resolve the bound seed findings at research-design level: complete covariance and deterministic support, anchored information preservation, geometric versus full-past innovations, true-point versus full-set coverage, and fixed-q fibre support with convex-hull and uncertain-anchor caveats.
assumptions_used: Scope is research/design handoff and bounded reference experiments; no production or scientific admission.
reproduction: Expand Cov(Yj+1-KjYj,Yk+1-KkYk) into four terms. For C=I3, eigenvalues of HCH^T are 1 and 3; dropping cross-step terms yields .5 Z1^2+1.5 Z2^2.
For the anchored transform, reconstruct Y recursively without inverting K.
On xi in C all defined f_t(xi) belong to the same outer images; this is not the event that every observationally equivalent xi lies in C.
Use LqLq*=Mq/3 to split STF3 into Rqv and ker(Lq); Cauchy-Schwarz gives the support, while support alone returns the convex hull.
